prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (alias Morrowick; collection/switching), export connection to Grid Interface Relay (external). Out of scope: public grid beyond connection; non-farm port ops. Architecture separates offshore equipment, services, shore decisions; interfaces have defined responsibilities for change management; supervisory functions distinct from planning/human coordination; personnel retain authority for procedural, safety and engineering judgment. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; produces Pitch Deviation Notice), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone. Substation: Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor. Shore/ops: SCADA Gateway (alias Juniper Vale; supervisory data boundary), Shore Control Room (alias Amber Quay; monitoring/coordination), Maintenance Planning Engine (alias Thistle Crown; supports Duty Planner), Fleet Dispatch Console (alias Sable Orchard; shared view of vessel assignments, movements, dispatch status for Marine Coordinator). Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (alias Kestrel Bay; transports authorized personnel, routine tools shore-offshore), Daughter Craft (short-range transfers when plan/conditions permit), Service Operations Vessel (longer presence, onboard support); Helideck. Personnel Tracking Console (accurate view of offshore personnel), North/South Access Scanners. Warehouse System (alias Mosslight; records stock, prepares equipment/consumables), Spares Hub. Enabling: Work Permit Portal, Cybersecurity Gateway (security boundary for connected services), comms, fire protection, backup power. Actors: SCADA Engineer; Control Engineer; Duty Planner (daily priorities with input from Field Supervisor and Maintenance Planning Engine); Marine Coordinator (aligns vessels with crew readiness, port access, work locations; coordinates CTV, SOV, Daughter Craft); Vessel Master (authority for navigation, vessel safety, transfer go/no-go; assesses conditions before/during voyage); Weather Analyst (reviews forecasts, advises Marine Coordinator); Storekeeper (checks materials vs stock, replenishment with Spares Hub); Port Agent (vessel calls, crew access, staged cargo); technicians, vessel crews. External: Weather Service (alias Pale Lantern; produces Squall Window Bulletin), Metocean Buoy, grid ops, ports, suppliers, emergency services. Requirements: work authorized, hazards controlled, personnel/vessels accounted; prevent pollution, minimize marine disturbance, prompt incident response. Modes: commissioning, normal service, planned maintenance, unplanned maintenance, major

Document units:
S095: The HSE Officer verifies that work arrangements account for applicable safety controls and personnel responsibilities.
S096: The Field Supervisor coordinates task execution offshore and keeps the Duty Planner informed of changes to work progress.
S097: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S098: The operating organization uses defined handoffs so that dispatch, marine judgment, work supervision, and stores control remain accountable functions.
S099: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S100: This section defines how offshore environmental observations and protected operational networks support safe farm operations.
S101: The Metocean Buoy is designated Copper Finch for operational reference.
S102: The Metocean Buoy measures wind speed and direction, wave height and period, current, air temperature, and barometric pressure.
S103: Sensors are selected and mounted to limit exposure to spray, icing, vibration, and corrosion.
S104: An onboard logger timestamps observations and retains a local history during intermittent communications.
S105: The Vessel AIS Receiver produces a Position Quality Flag when position integrity checks fail or confidence falls below its configured threshold.
S106: The Weather Service uses validated environmental observations in forecast products for offshore planning.
S107: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast limitations and identifies conditions that may affect vessel access or turbine work.
S108: Measurement intervals and alarm thresholds are configured to support both trend analysis and timely operational decisions.
S109: Time synchronization and sensor health are checked as part of routine monitoring.
S110: The Cybersecurity Gateway is designated Quiet Harbor for operational reference.
S111: The Cybersecurity Gateway establishes a controlled boundary between authorized shore-side services and offshore operational networks.
S112: The boundary permits only approved protocols, destinations, and service accounts.
S113: External connectivity is denied by default and enabled only for documented operational needs.
S114: The SCADA Gateway remains responsible for supervisory communications within its defined control scope.
S115: Administrative access requires authenticated individual accounts and role-based authorization.
S116: Privileged sessions are time limited, logged, and reviewed against approved maintenance activity.
S117: The Cybersecurity Analyst monitors gateway events for unusual access patterns and configuration changes.
S118: Loss of the security boundary places remote administrative functions in a restricted state without bypassing local protective controls.
S119: Security events are retained in protected logs for investigation and audit.
S120: Network segmentation limits the effect of a compromised endpoint and supports controlled restoration of service.
